title: Neural circuit mechanisms for steering control in walking Drosophila
source_locator: Fig. 8A-C; Results, 'Contributions of single descending neuron types to steering behavior'; Methods, 'Stochastic ReaChR expression'
quote: In the flies with unilateral expression, we found that light evoked a small average steering bias in the ipsilateral direction
mapping_basis: Paper names the neuron DNa02, which is itself a MANC type in type_list.csv; driver SS00730 maps to DNa02 in driver_lines.csv.
stimulation: 617 nm orange light from above the head, symmetric, 68 uW/mm2, 0.5 s every 11 s, 150 trials
type_coverage: unilateral: one DNa02 copy (left-only 9, right-only 8 of 73 brains)
sensory_condition: on spherical treadmill (air-floated ball), head cuticle intact, no dissection
coordination_notes: Only ball rotational velocity measured; legs not tracked in this experiment.
penetrance: Small ipsilateral rotational bias on average; mean outside 95% CI of bootstrap from bilateral siblings (Fig. 8B,C); most but not all individual flies positive in Fig. 8C
n_flies_note: Fig. 8B legend: mean of 16/17 flies (uni/bilateral ReaChR)
notes: Flies were walking on the ball when light was delivered, so per protocol section 3 the turn is coded under effect_on_walking and leg-rhythm fields are not_assessed. Off-target expression of SS00730 in optic lobe and VNC cells is stated in Fig. 8-figure supplement 2 legend (shown with GtACR1/GFP). Forward-velocity effects were confounded by visual startle and not interpreted by the authors.

title: Neural circuit mechanisms for steering control in walking Drosophila
source_locator: Fig. 8A-C (bilateral ReaChR group); Results, 'Contributions of single descending neuron types to steering behavior' (forward velocity: data not shown)
quote: These effects were likely due to visual startle, because they were indistinguishable in flies with unilateral expression, bilateral expression, and no expression
mapping_basis: Paper names the neuron DNa02, which is itself a MANC type in type_list.csv; driver SS00730 maps to DNa02 in driver_lines.csv.
stimulation: 617 nm orange light from above the head, symmetric, 68 uW/mm2, 0.5 s every 11 s, 150 trials
type_coverage: bilateral: both DNa02 copies (47 of 73 brains)
sensory_condition: on spherical treadmill (air-floated ball), head cuticle intact, no dissection
coordination_notes: Only ball velocities measured; legs not tracked.
penetrance: Bilateral flies served as the null distribution for directional bias (Fig. 8B,C, mean near 0); forward-velocity changes indistinguishable from no-expression flies (data not shown)
n_flies_note: Fig. 8B legend: mean of 16/17 flies (uni/bilateral ReaChR); Methods report bilateral expression in 47 of 73 brains
notes: Outcome differs from the unilateral condition, so a separate record per protocol section 1. Coded as no effect beyond controls because light-evoked forward-velocity changes matched no-expression flies; however the authors state they could not use this dataset to assess the effect of DNa02 activation on forward velocity due to visual startle, hence low confidence. Rotational data for bilateral flies used only with random right/left labels, so no direction-free turning measure was reported.
